ethnobotany: Kivuli, dawa ya malaria na ngozi, kukinga wadudu. Known as the 'village pharmacy'.
funFact: Mti huu unaitwa 'kituo cha dawa kijijini' kwa sababu sehemu zake zote ni dawa.
climateImpact: Highly drought tolerant. Survives in harsh conditions.

description: A tall, slender tree widely planted along roadsides and in urban gardens. Provides excellent shade without damaging pavements.
ethnobotany: Mapambo na kivuli, mti huu hauna mizizi inayoharibu miundo.
funFact: Mti huu una umbo la piramidi na hukua hadi mita 18 juu.

description: A fast-growing tree used for shade, fodder, and timber. Common in Morogoro Municipality and urban areas of Tanzania.
ethnobotany: Kivuli, malisho kwa mifugo, mbao kwa kuni, majani ni mbolea.
funFact: Mti huu unaweza kukua mita 2-3 kwa mwaka na ni bora kwa kurejesha udongo.

description: A fast-growing tree providing shade and edible fruits. Common in urban areas and settlements across Tanzania.
ethnobotany: Kivuli, matunda huliwa, gome hutumika kwa dawa.
funFact: Matunda ya mti huu yana ladha tamu na hutumiwa kutengeneza vinywaji.

description: A popular shade tree in Zanzibar and coastal cities. Provides biocooling benefits and is well-adapted to urban environments.
ethnobotany: Kivuli kikubwa, matunda huliwa, majani hutumika kwa dawa za ini.
funFact: Majani ya mkwaju yanageuka kuwa mekundu kabla ya kuanguka, kutoa rangi nzuri mijini.
climateImpact: Salt tolerant. Grows well near coast.

description: A popular ornamental tree in towns, providing quick shade. Recommended for fuel and pole production in dry areas of Tanzania.
ethnobotany: Firewood, poles, timber (furniture), medicine (leaves), bee forage, shade, ornamental, insecticide.
funFact: The tree can provide quick shade and has fragrant lilac flowers with a dark purple center.
climateImpact: Drought resistant. Grows on most soils.

description: One of the most common fruit and shade trees in urban areas. Provides food, shade, and cooling benefits in cities.
ethnobotany: Matunda huliwa, kivuli, majani hutumika kwa sherehe.
funFact: Maembe yamekuwa yakilimwa kwa zaidi ya miaka 4,000.

description: A large shade tree planted in urban squares, schools, and settlements. Provides excellent cooling and shade.
ethnobotany: Kivuli kikubwa, mbao kwa samani, majani kama malisho.
funFact: Mbungu wa mzingiri unatoa sauti ya kigegenezi ukikauka, hivyo jina 'woman's tongue tree'.

description: A common street tree in Dar es Salaam. Has fragrant white flowers that open at night and provides good shade.
ethnobotany: Planted for ornament and shade. Flowers have a pleasant fragrance.
funFact: The flowers open mostly at night and have a sweet, jasmine-like fragrance.

description: A hardy shrub or tree with bright yellow flowers. Suitable for home yards, open spaces, and hedging in urban areas.
ethnobotany: Medicinal plant, fruits are edible, used for hedging. Good for planting in home yards.
funFact: The bright yellow flowers attract birds and bees, enhancing urban biodiversity.
climateImpact: Drought tolerant. Grows in various soil types.

description: A shrub or small tree with bright yellow flowers and red sepals. Native to East Africa and popular as an ornamental plant.
ethnobotany: Planted for ornament. Attractive flowers and fruits.
funFact: The flowers are bright yellow with red sepals, making it a striking ornamental plant.

description: A shrub or small to medium tree with striking yellow flowers. Suitable for planting in town reserves and home gardens.
ethnobotany: Used for hedging and ornamental purposes. Attracts bees and birds.
funFact: The long fruit capsules remain on the tree after flowering, adding visual interest.

description: A shrub or branched tree up to 20 m tall. Suitable for planting in home gardens and town reserves.
ethnobotany: Provides shade and ornamental value. Wood used for construction.
funFact: This tree is native to coastal East Africa and is well-adapted to urban environments.
climateImpact: Salt tolerant. Grows well near coast.

description: A flowering coastal tree up to 10 m in height. Good for planting in town reserves and public spaces.
ethnobotany: Provides shade and ornamental yellow flowers. Wood used for construction.
funFact: The yellow flowers are beautiful and attract pollinators to urban gardens.
climateImpact: Salt tolerant. Grows well near coast.

description: A deciduous tree or shrub up to 20m tall. Suitable for planting in open spaces such as school yards or hospital precincts.
ethnobotany: Good shade tree. Wood for construction and furniture.
funFact: Provides excellent shade and is ideal for large open urban spaces.

description: A shrub or small tree with attractive edible fruits. Suitable for home gardens, public open spaces, and town reserves.
ethnobotany: Fruits eaten fresh, leaves and roots used for treating fever.
funFact: The fruit is similar to soursop and is loved for its sweet, creamy taste.

description: A medium-sized tree suitable for planting in town reserves and urban green spaces.
ethnobotany: Provides shade and timber. Fruits attract birds to urban gardens.
funFact: This tree is native to coastal East Africa and is well-suited to urban environments.

description: A small to medium-sized deciduous tree up to 7 m in height. Suitable for urban planting.
ethnobotany: Medicinal uses. Attractive flowers and pods.
funFact: The long pods are distinctive and remain on the tree for a long time.

description: A rare tree that grows very well and fast, with sweet-smelling flowers. Suitable for town reserves and botanical gardens.
ethnobotany: Ornamental tree with fragrant flowers. Timber for carving.
funFact: The flowers have a sweet fragrance that attracts pollinators to urban gardens.

description: A herbaceous climber with medicinal properties. Suitable for home gardens and urban green spaces.
ethnobotany: Medicinal uses. Attractive growth habit for vertical gardens.
funFact: This climber adds vertical interest to urban gardens and provides habitat for insects.

description: A palm species found only in Tanzania. Fronds are not heavy, hence not dangerous when they fall. Suitable for town reserves.
ethnobotany: Ornamental palm for urban landscaping.
funFact: This palm is endemic to Tanzania and is safe for urban planting as its fronds are not heavy.

description: A native cycad species that deserves wider cultivation. Good for home and office gardens and road islands.
ethnobotany: Ornamental plant with attractive form. Good for urban landscaping.
funFact: This cycad is a living fossil and adds a prehistoric element to urban gardens.

description: An evergreen shrub or small tree up to 9 m high. Fruits attract birds; flowers attract insects. Suitable for town reserves, home yards, and botanical gardens.
ethnobotany: Fruits attract birds. Used as a toothbrush tree (mswaki).
funFact: The branches are traditionally used as a toothbrush, hence the name 'mswaki'.

description: A succulent shrub usually 3-5 m in height. Useful in hedging and as a living fence in urban areas.
ethnobotany: Used for hedging and as a living fence. Low maintenance.
funFact: This plant is extremely drought tolerant and can survive with minimal water.

description: A shrub or small tree with attractive fruit. Useful in hedging and border-planting in urban gardens.
ethnobotany: Attractive fruit. Used for hedging and border-planting.
funFact: The fruits are edible and attract birds to urban gardens.

description: A bush or small tree that grows easily and is low maintenance. White berries loved by birds. Good for planting in town reserves and along rivers.
ethnobotany: Low maintenance plant. Berries attract birds to urban areas.
funFact: The white berries are loved by birds, making this plant excellent for urban wildlife gardens.

description: An ornamental shrub with yellow resin. Good for home and botanical gardens in urban areas.
ethnobotany: Ornamental shrub for home and botanical gardens.
funFact: The yellow resin is distinctive and adds ornamental value to gardens.

description: A plant that should replace the commonly grown Chinese hibiscus. Always flowering with showy flowers. Suitable for road islands and home gardens.
ethnobotany: Ornamental plant with showy, always-blooming flowers.
funFact: This native hibiscus is always flowering and has showy, attractive flowers.

localName: Micoma Mkoche / East African Doum Palm
description: A uniquely branched palm, unlike most palms which are not branched. Suitable for planting in town reserves and urban landscapes.
ethnobotany: Ornamental palm for urban landscaping. Provides shade and visual interest.
funFact: This palm is unique because it branches, unlike most other palm species.
climateImpact: Drought tolerant. Grows well in coastal urban areas.
